root_idea.summary: A root centered on breaking, crumbling, and reducing something into fragments, with an associated notion of twisting or severing.
root_idea.development: Material broken down by hand or force becomes رُفَاتٌ, while the same semantic orientation extends to things breaking off, becoming severed, or figuratively decaying.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic noun رُفَاتٌ rather than the inflected Quranic surface form.

senses.definition: Crumbled, scattered fragments or particles, especially the remains of old, decayed bones and more generally dry material broken into small pieces.
senses.usage_conditions: A mass noun used in the Quran in coordination with عِظَامٌ (bones), describing material reduced to fragments; attested at 17:49 and 17:98.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break, crush, bruise, bray, pound, or crumble something into small pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I transitive usage, including the breaking or crushing of bones and other solid things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to relieve or break the intensity of thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended figurative construction used specifically of water relieving thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break something extensively or into many pieces.
To dishonour, despise, or condemn someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended figurative use of Form II, expressing contempt or degradation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become broken, crushed, bruised, brayed, pounded, or broken into pieces; also to break or become broken off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IX usage can be intransitive or transitive; the breaking-off construction is attested of a rope.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Straw, especially straw that has been trodden or threshed and cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage distinct from the Quranic noun رُفَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A breaker or crusher: one who breaks, crushes, bruises, brays, pounds, or crumbles things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent-noun usage referring to a person who performs the breaking action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or manner of breaking, crushing, or reducing something to pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun naming the manner or method of the breaking action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By metaphorical extension, something severed piece by piece, such as a broken rope, or something decayed that is restored, including neglected merits or actions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative applications extend the physical idea of fragmentation to a rope broken into sections and to qualities or actions that have fallen into decay.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broken, crushed, or broken into pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective describing something subjected to the breaking or crushing action.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I breaking, crushing, and crumbling action is represented.
The extended water-and-thirst construction is represented.
The intensive Form II breaking action is represented.
The figurative Form II sense of dishonouring or despising is represented.
The intransitive and transitive Form IX breaking and breaking-off uses are represented.
The noun for a mode or manner of breaking is represented.
The Quran-attested physical fragment sense and the recorded figurative extensions are represented.

cautions: The public headword is the dictionary citation form رُفَاتٌ; the two QAC occurrences appear in the accusative surface form رُفَاتًا. Historical Quran citation notation in the lexical evidence is not used as a modern verse location; the examples use the independently supplied QAC locations.
